content.thinking:
I'm planning the file structure carefully, setting up imports for the builder, paint helpers, path utilities, RNG, texture, and shading kits, then outlining the default export function with its metadata and root return.

Now I'm sketching the treant's overall design: a towering ~4-4.5m body with a trunk torso, thick root-like legs, branch arms, a trunk-face head, and a leafy crown with glowing amber eyes, moss, mushrooms, vines, and worn metal bands for Warcraft-style detailing. I'm defining the bark paint by layering cel-shaded grain textures with an explicit dark shadow tone, plus a moss paint that swaps in based on vertical normal position.

I'm working out a limb-building helper using catmull-rom paths swept with tapered radii to construct the branch-like arms and legs.

I'm laying out the leg positions with hip, knee, and foot points along y-up, z-forward axes, tapering radii for a root-like leg shape, then adding toe sweeps radiating from the foot with tapered round caps, and shaping a heel blob with a sphere primitive to ground the foot naturally.

Now I'm sketching the torso as a swept spline from pelvis to chest, varying the ellipse radii to widen at the chest and narrow at the hips, with a pelvis sphere anchoring the base before starting on head placement.

The head sits hunched forward with its own scaled sphere, and I'm working out the facial features — brow ridges, a root-like nose, glowing amber eyes set in dark sockets, a dark mouth, and a mossy beard made from hanging cards and vine sweeps — positioning the eyes symmetrically off the head's center point.

Calculating eye socket depth...

Adding fine mouth path detail, then shifting to design antler branches with leaf textures in an autumn-green palette, and planning thick arms with long ground-reaching hands starting from the shoulders.

Now I'm working out the gnarled root-like fingers and palm geometry for the hands, plus mossy burl pauldrons on the oversized heroic shoulders, with branch forks sprouting leaf cards upward from the shoulders and elbows.

I need a helper to sweep branch paths and place leaf cards along them using frame-based orientation, importing the frame utility so cards face outward correctly along each branch.

For foliage, I'm planning clustered leaf cards at branch tips with randomized offsets and outward-facing axes, plus low-poly icosahedron blobs underneath for solid cel-shaded leaf clumps, sizing and leaning the cards so they read naturally as foliage.

I'm estimating around 320 cards across 8 canopy clumps, keeping triangle counts low per card. Now I'm thinking through bark texture — adding vertical ridge rods along the torso surface, computing their positions manually along the elliptical cross-section since a standard sweep won't wrap correctly.

Defining torso path and ridge placement...

Working out the ridge cross-section orientation: since the torso path runs mostly vertical, I'm resolving which axis (x or z) the binormal/normal map to, settling on binormal along x and normal along -z for consistency, then sampling ridge points with small random wobble and a tapering sweep radius like [0.05, 0.035, 0.04].

For decoration I'm thinking Warcraft-treant style: bark coloring with dark/highlight variation, glowing amber rune carvings on the chest, shelf mushrooms, vine wraps, hanging moss, and a bird's nest with eggs on the shoulder for storytelling detail. I'm placing a glowing rune plane on the chest front, positioning it using the torso path's point around t≈0.7 to figure out the z-depth where the chest surface sits.

I'm figuring out how to apply the rune decal properly using a decal function that projects texture onto the torso surface, picking a point near the chest and giving it a glow effect so the amber runes read as emissive. I'm also thinking about adding glowing amber eyes, and a root-like loincloth or draping roots radiating from the hips down to the ground for extra organic detail.

For the legs, I'm planning knee burls and ankle roots with bark-textured ridges, using layered grain-based paint functions for lit and shadowed bark tones combined through a cel shading function, then adding patchy moss on upward-facing surfaces using noise to scatter moss patches over the bark.

Writing bark paint logic...

Planning more helper utilities...

Still writing SVG leaf shape code...

I'm thinking through leaf card frames pointing outward from clump centers, and sketching a clump function that builds overlapping blob shapes from icosahedron parts for leaf coloring.

Writing branch sweep helper code...

Simplifying to a basic two-radius rod for the twigs instead of a full sweep, then adding smaller clumps at the tips. For the shoulders, I'm planning lumpy burl shapes using scaled icosahedrons positioned to suggest heroic pauldrons over the torso.

Adding small root spikes on the pauldrons for texture, plus moss caps and a mushroom detail on one shoulder—using a hemisphere scaled cone shape with red coloring and white spotted paint for a classic fantasy toadstool look, maybe nesting it near the shoulder joint.

On the other shoulder I'm placing a small nest ring with a few pale blue eggs inside, using a flattened torus rotated flat and stretched spheres for the eggs. Then I'm planning a vine that wraps diagonally around the torso, computing a spiral path of points following an elliptical radius with rising height, to give the figure an organic, overgrown feel with small leaves along the way.

Beyond that, I'm also sketching hanging moss strands under the chin, using angled card frames positioned along the jaw arc to create a beard-like cascade of greenery draping down toward the chest.

I want to add a chin burl bump, forked antler-branch crowns on the head sides in place of ears, bark brow ridges with dark eye sockets, and burl-sphere cheekbones for texture. Then I'm figuring out the hand geometry -- positioning wrist and palm spheres, and starting to lay out finger placement spreading from the palm's front edge.

Still writing finger curl geometry...

Still placing foot and toe geometry...

Now I'm working out the torso base and the branching crown structure—back branches rising from the upper back, side branches from the shoulders sweeping outward and up, and antler-like crown branches from the head, aiming for a total creature height around 5.6 units.

I need the head hunched forward so the beard overlaps the chest naturally — shifting head z to 0.6 and y to 3.55, then recalculating the eye and mouth positions relative to that new offset.

Still writing mouth curve coordinates...

Now I'm placing the remaining facial features: small spike teeth near the lower jaw, a nose spike protruding forward, cheek burls as small spheres, and brow rods positioned above the eyes.

I'm setting up the eye socket with a dark recessed sphere, an amber glow sphere, and a brighter yellow pupil layered inside, then moving to a mossy crown tuft on top and a rune decal design for the chest.

For the belt, I'm sketching a woven vine rope with bronze druid trim details -- rivets and a gold medallion -- plus torus-shaped wrist bands positioned along the arm path to mimic gorget bands in a worn, Blizzard-style finish.

Calculating belt geometry...

I'll place a medallion at the front and keep radius loose enough to tolerate slight ellipse mismatches. For decoration I'm skipping bark plates and birds, but adding small mushrooms on the shoulders, back, and knee using a helper function with a thin stem and a hemisphere cap.

Still writing mushroom code...

I'm skipping ground elements since this is creature-only, and settling on a bark palette with base, shadow, and moss highlight tones.

Now I'm expanding the full color palette with leaf greens, amber, bronze, cream, mushroom red, and mud tones, plus defining leaf texture variants and designing a wavy moss strand SVG shape to hang from the creature's shoulders and arms.

I'm placing hanging moss at the pauldron edges, chin, elbows, and pelvis belt, with no additional ground cover needed. Setting up the file's imports for the builder, paint utilities (mottle for moss, spots for mushroom caps, grain for bark texture), toon shading kit, and seeded randomness for deterministic generation.

Defining the build function structure with meta export and torso radius helper, then setting up bark and moss paint definitions using layered grain and mottle textures with toon shading.

Adding darker bark variants, mouth interior shading, and a glow wrapper for certain parts; now working out decal placement for a rune marking on the torso surface, checking that the sweep geometry supports decal targeting at the right position and orientation.

I'm also sketching the cards function signature for leaf-like or decorative elements, with parameters controlling size, lean, bend, spin, and randomness for texture variation.

I'm estimating triangle counts for leaf clumps and their bend segments, then thinking through the clump shape using icosahedron geometry and a mottled green color treatment for the leaf blobs.

Writing clump function code...

Still writing twig placement logic...

Now sketching a mushroom helper function that builds a base, cap stem, and dome shape using scaled radii off a lean direction.

Confirming the torus lies flat in the XY plane with Z as its axis, so I'll sample the arm paths to position bronze bands. For the pauldron spikes, I'm using radiating horn shapes with a base, direction, length, and radius for a bark-like root texture, plus capsules for burl details.

Now I'm adding glowing amber sap crack details—jagged sweep lines on the chest and arms using an amber glow effect, and placing rune decals on both pauldron spheres with offset positions along the outer ellipsoid surface to keep them visible.

I also want to add hanging moss clumps underneath each pauldron, generating a ring of points around the pauldron's underside using circular angle offsets to scatter moss card frames naturally.

More moss points around the chin, elbows, and belt. For the rune design, I'm sketching an SVG glyph with concentric amber rings and a simple vertical-and-chevron rune pattern, sized so the stroke scales cleanly at 192px. I also want to give the eyes a subtle glowing amber sphere effect.

Now I'm working out the geometry for limbs and hands -- looping through left/right sides, defining arm sweep paths, and placing finger and thumb points with slight offsets so they curve naturally toward the palm, plus adding claw spikes at the fingertips.

I'm sweeping each finger as a curved tube with tapering radius and rounded-to-pointed caps, then adding wrist and ankle bands as torus shapes positioned along the limb paths, and starting to plan spiky ridge details along the back.

Still placing ridge sweeps...

Now sketching the torso sweep with a rounded bark-colored path and cleaning up unused imports before finalizing the radius function's type signature.
